narrative.value: Military analysis treats the direct US-Israel-Iran exchanges as a structural break, questioning which deterrence assumptions survive and what force postures follow.
Diplomatic coverage asks whether negotiation frameworks and nuclear containment can be rebuilt once escalation has burned through existing channels.
Economic analysis is absent from the current source base, leaving sanctions pressure and workaround capacity unexamined this cycle.
Human-cost coverage remains thin, appearing mainly in war round-ups; who absorbs the civilian toll of escalation is largely unaddressed.
Regional commentary focuses on endgame scenarios, asking which alignments and proxy relationships hold as the conflict reshapes the map.
How should deterrence, diplomacy, and regional alignments be rebuilt after the war?

The corpus frames the 2026 US-Israel-Iran war as a structural break. Military analysis treats direct strikes as ending decades of deterrence assumptions, while diplomatic coverage questions whether any negotiation framework or nuclear containment model survives the escalation. Human-cost and regional-alignment coverage remains thin, and the economic dimension is absent from the current cache — a coverage gap to monitor next cycle.
